title: 2025 Annual Australian Measles and Rubella Genotyping Surveillance Program Report.
abstract: Molecular characterisation is a critical component of Australia's measles and rubella surveillance systems, supporting outbreak investigations, identifying sources of infection, and providing evidence for the continued maintenance of Australia's measles and rubella elimination status. This annual report summarises measles and rubella molecular epidemiology in Australia during 2025 and evaluates the utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) for measles surveillance. In 2025, there were 181 confirmed measles cases notified in Australia, representing a 217.5% increase on the number notified in 2024. Measles virus genotypes B3 and D8 were detected, together with 21 vaccine-associated genotype A cases. Genotype B3 predominated during the first half of the year and was largely associated with importations from Vietnam, whereas genotype D8 predominated during the second half of the year and was primarily associated with importations from Indonesia. Thirty-one epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks were identified, comprising 13 genotype B3 outbreaks and 17 genotype D8 outbreaks. The discriminatory power and concordance with epidemiological data in the context of outbreak investigations was substantially greater for WGS data than for conventional N450-based genotyping. Viruses sharing the same N450-based distinct sequence identifier (DSid) differed by up to 33 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for genotype B3 and 36 SNPs for genotype D8, whereas genomes obtained from epidemiologically linked cases differed by a maximum of four SNPs. Despite increased national case numbers in 2025, available molecular and epidemiological evidence indicated that cases were associated with importations or import-related transmission events, with no evidence of sustained endemic measles transmission. Rubella activity remained extremely low, with no rubella virus detections identified among 157 specimens tested by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and only two notified cases nationally, neither of which had material available for genotyping. These findings support the continued absence of endemic measles and rubella transmission in Australia and highlight the value of WGS for enhancing measles surveillance and outbreak investigations.

title: Molecular epidemiology of influenza A (H5N6) viruses from human infections in Jiangsu Province, China.
abstract: Human infections with avian influenza A (H5N6) have been reported with increasing frequency in recent years. This study aims to systematically characterize the epidemiological and molecular characteristics of human H5N6 infections in Jiangsu Province, China, in order to inform epidemic prevention and control strategies and support clinical diagnosis. Human cases of H5N6 infections were collected in Jiangsu Province. Clinical and epidemiological data of the cases were investigated and analyzed. Phylogenetic and evolutionary analyses were performed using the Jiangsu-derived viral strains together with publicly available reference sequences, employing MEGA and BEAST, and R packages. Between November 2018 and the present, five laboratory-confirmed human cases of avian influenza A (H5N6) infection were reported in Jiangsu Province. The ages of the patients ranged from 6 to 81 years. All close contacts tested negative for H5N6 nucleic acid. Environmental investigations revealed only one sample positive for H5N6 nucleic acid. Phylogenetic analysis showed that all hemagglutination genes clustered within evolutionary branch 2.3.4.4h and 2.3.4.4b. The median time to the most recent common ancestor of the Jiangsu viruses was estimated to be December 2009 for the HA gene and July 2014 for the neuraminidase gene. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiological and molecular characteristics of human H5N6 infections in Jiangsu Province. No evidence of human-to-human transmission was found among the infected cases and their close contacts. However, the ongoing genetic evolution of H5N6 viruses may increase the risk of human infection and warrants continued surveillance.

title: Genomic epidemiology of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading infectious killer worldwide. Brazil is among the 30 high-burden TB countries, however, genomic surveillance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains remains limited. We analyzed a convenience sample of 350 clinical isolates collected between 2016 and 2021 in metropolitan Rio de Janeiro to investigate genomic diversity, drug resistance and transmission dynamics. Among the isolates, 302 were phenotypically susceptible, while 48 showed resistance to at least one drug, including 35 multidrug-resistant (MDR) cases. Whole-genome sequencing predictions showed high concordance with phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (rifampicin 99%, isoniazid 99%, ethambutol 98%, streptomycin 97%). The most common resistance mutations were katG Ser315Thr and rpoB Ser450Leu. All isolates belonged to Lineage 4, predominantly sub-lineages 4.1 (Haarlem) and 4.3 (Latin American-Mediterranean). Despite incomplete sampling, genomic analysis identified 28 transmission clusters involving 23.2% of isolates, including a large MDR-TB cluster in the Tijuca neighborhood. Multi-year clusters indicated continued detection of closely related isolates over time, suggesting the persistence of related genomic lineages. No association was observed between resistance-associated mutations and treatment outcomes, although these analyses were likely underpowered to detect such associations. These findings highlight the need to strengthen genomic surveillance, molecular diagnostics, contact tracing, and treatment follow-up to control TB in the region.

title: Genomic epidemiology of CHIKV during the largest outbreak in Mainland China - implication for CHIKV intervention.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has caused recurrent epidemics across tropical and subtropical regions globally. In 2025, Guangdong, China, experienced the largest documented CHIKV outbreak in mainland China, with 23,464 reported cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities. We conducted integrated epidemiological, genomic, and phylodynamic analyses to investigate the outbreak's origins, transmission dynamics, and CHIKV lineage evolution. The Guangdong strain belongs to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype, Middle African lineage (ECSA-MAL) - one of several CHIKV lineages co-circulating globally in 2025; a long internal branch separates ECSA-MAL from previously sequenced relatives, indicating substantial surveillance gaps in endemic regions. Phylodynamic analysis using a local molecular clock model estimated that the viral introduction occurred within a narrow window in early April 2025 (95% HPD: March 26-April 12), suggesting a 2.5-month period of cryptic transmission prior to detection. The prolonged silent phase aligns with vector dynamics: the Mosquito Ovitrap Index in the outbreak town of Beijiao, Foshan, stayed low in April (3.0) before surging to 9.0 through July - consistent with suppressed early transmission followed by seasonal amplification. Human migration from the two epidemic epicenters was moderately associated with the spatial distribution of cases (Spearman ρ around 0.5), while mosquito ecology may constrain spatial spread. Phylowave analysis on global circulating strains identified 33 lineage-defining mutations across 14 sublineages, concentrated in NSP3, E1 and E2. Four of these have been experimentally validated as adaptive mutations. This study demonstrates the critical need for enhanced genomic surveillance during pre-peak months and underscores the importance of monitoring adaptive mutations across diverse ecological regions.
